newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet sell-off could be delayed MD warns.
newsitem.headline: Stet sell-off could be delayed MD warns.

text.p: The privatisation of Italian state telecom holding Stet, slated for the spring of 1997, will be delayed unless parliament rapidly approves a bill setting up a watchdog body for the sector, Stet managing director Ernesto Pascale said on Friday.

"If the watchdog authority has not been approved by the end of November, there will not be time to float Stet in February or March," Pascale told reporters after meeting European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert.
The watchdog authority bill is tied to a draft law covering television ownership, which is hotly disputed by the opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance bloc in parliament.

The government has said it hopes the whole package will be approved by the end of the year but Pascale said he wanted Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico to strip out the section relating to the regulatory body and hasten its progress through parliament.
Van Miert said on Thursday that Italy had asked for a one year extension on the terms of a 1993 agreement on reducing debt at state industrial holding IRI, which controls Stet.
IRI has said it will use proceeds from the Stet sale to reduce its debt level.
"I think (the government) is afraid that the watchdog bill won't be approved in time and want to give themselves room for a second (selling) opportunity," Van Miert told reporters on Friday.
